That is, your employees need to think it's an evil sin to sell IP to China. 

And that your coworkers will rat you out in a heartbeat if they think you're doing something like that."

"One of the biggest things that happened in modern American history is the mutual discovery of tech and government. 

In the 1990s, companies would say, I'm not an American company, I'm a global company, and nowhere was that stronger than in the world of tech, where Google has no boundaries.

Today, tech is actually the locus of international great power competition. 

China's attempt to build a technosphere that can dominate the American technosphere is critical to your business, but also to the American state, to power and independence. 

So much to the surprise of both the tech world and the political world, they've been driven in on each other, and there's a kind of re-nationalization of tech.

If you're a legacy multinational, free trade is the essence of your business. I need financial markets, labor markets, and manufactured good markets that are seamless and open. 

But if you're a tech company, you don't. Google is not importing and exporting a lot of goods. 

You're much more concerned about security of supply chain, security of intellectual property."

This story underscores that privacy remains one of the core unsolved problems in AI.

We feel intuitively that AIs are our closest confidantes. We routinely share our secrets, vulnerabilities, and most valuable work with our AIs. AIs have become an extension of our conversations with ourselves; like the innermost chambers of our minds.

But legally, that's not how it works. 

According to the law, you have sent your data to a third party, and according to the third party doctrine, you have lost your right to 4th amendment protections. Your data can be looked at, pored over, it can be retrieved without a search warrant, it must be handed over in legal discovery, and so on. It is no longer yours. Legally, you have willingly given it away.

We need to fix this. We need to pass strong privacy laws around AI usage, and harmonize them with stuff like email (which the Supreme Court has only recently definitively established is legally protected).

This is a big part of the reason why we invested into @AskVenice, which is fully private by default, even for consumers. They take an Apple-like ideological stance that AI usage should be private and belong solely to the user. I believe all of American society is going to move in this direction. If not now, then soon.

a16z's Anish Acharya on the AI era's "permanent underclass" and the reasons he doesn't buy it:

"It's a funny dark fantasy that we seem to have as Silicon Valley collectively. Things have never been better, really by almost every measure."

"By how distributed all the opportunities are, by the kind of technology we have access to, to the types of ambition we're allowed to have, and to the number of companies independently working on things that are winning."

"The last era of tech was a lot more centralized... If you look at what's happening now, every part of the stack, there's not even two relevant players. There's like 20."

"You've heard all the economic data... And of course job postings are higher than they've ever been, as well as programmers. So I don't know that the empirical data bears it out."

"RSI, recursive self-improvement, is a fun term to throw around. But if you ask the most sophisticated individuals at the labs, it's not actually RSI that's occurring, which could lead to some runaway winner... It's autocatalytic effects, which just means you're using the new technology to improve your process, but it's not truly recursive."

"So everything from the most empirical to the most technical points in the other direction, and yet we can't seem to let go of this fantasy."

@illscience w/ @lennysan

Leading indicators point to higher US inflation.

The ISM Services Prices Paid Index rose +2.3 points in August, to 72.6, its highest since July 2022.

Since February, the index has risen +9.6 points, its largest 6-month increase since May 2025.

Historically, this metric has led CPI inflation and core PCE inflation by ~6 months.

If the historical relationship holds, the current reading suggests CPI could rise to as high as 6.0% in the coming months, from 3.4% in July.

At the same time, this implies core PCE could increase above 4.0%, from July’s reported 3.3%.

Inflation pressures are intensifying in the US.

MetaDAO is rethinking capital formation for startups.

Most launchpads help projects raise money and then step away. MetaDAO uses token markets to govern some of the capital decisions that come next.

Capital raised through the platform enters a DAO treasury with spending limits. When a project seeks more funding or wants to change how its treasury is used, it can submit a proposal to a decision market. Traders estimate what the token would be worth if the proposal passes or fails, and the difference between those prices determines the outcome.

Four approved proposals have raised another $13.34M for MetaDAO itself since launch. Two passed only after earlier versions failed and the terms changed. The same process has returned remaining capital to investors when projects were wound down.

This model depends on active tokenholders. One restructuring passed with only seven wallets and less than $700 in volume. Across 12 launches, a median 52% of allocated wallets sold some tokens within seven days. It remains unclear whether launch recipients will become long-term owners.

The opportunity is larger than a better token launchpad. If tokenization becomes a meaningful way to fund operating businesses, MetaDAO could develop into a founder platform for a new generation of companies raising capital online.

- $67.7 billion (+33% revision) for 2026
- $131.4 billion (+81% revision) for 2027
- $148.5 billion (+115% revision) for 2028

For $NVDA Rubin Ultra, GS increased its modeled optical modules per GPU:

1.6T: 0 -> 2
3.2T: 3 -> 5 

GS also raised their 1.6T and above forecast for 2027 by 61%... so that's also very material, with 80% silicon photonics penetration rate estimated. 

So more optical content per chip = a lot more CW lasers, more SOI substrates, happy optical companies.

Okay I know this is US time and this is a Taiwan stock...

But I really am starting to think $ESMT (3006) can cook like $SNDK. And I’m excited.

So hopefully in a few months, people can something say similar... 

FUN FACT CHAT: 

Did you know.. 1 old DDR2 memory chip is.. ~$0.96? (from LCSC data) 

Obviously different per spec since some can be $2.5... 

But if you 3x ASP Hike this. 

That's a whole... ~$2 added to final BOM cost. 

So about the same cost as a $COST hot dog. 

It goes into things like a D-Link security camera, maybe like $33 final cost... 

and adds like $2. (which people won't mind)

But... 3X ASP hike to ESMT? Is very, very material. 

That's just for one product category, and there's many others from SLC NAND (eg. +120–170% H2) to NOR Flash products for H2 ASP hike projections. 

And my favorite thing is, they've already shown they're willing to partake in the price hike games (seems like there's a long way to go)…

Currently they make ~$111M net income a month from July earnings ($2.8B MC), which annualized is like ~2.1X P/E. *I have positions.

So... I think $ESMT has room to cook like masterchef Sandisk. 

TLDR:
- Repeated rounds of price hiking = seems absurd for the company's net income... but has potential due to starting low component cost. 

- Reminds me of early $SNDK but for other segments (legacy/niche memory).

The Carob Trust is launching an academic prize to be awarded to up to five researchers each year. Our goal is to incentivize the pursuit and publication of the truth wherever the facts may lead. 

Unfortunately today, many findings go unpublished as researchers fear blowback from colleagues, the university, or large swathes of the public because their findings reveal an uncomfortable truth. 

Our goal with the prize is to reward academic courage and excellence. We welcome your submissions. 

Info on The Carob Trust and details on the prize can be found at the links below. A summary follows:

https://t.co/oKcriZl7bi

https://t.co/Lb1PX6WiaL

The Carob Trust Prize for Academic Courage

Celebrating the Pursuit of Knowledge

•Mission: The Carob Trust Prize honors academics who pursue bold ideas that challenge prevailing orthodoxies—whether political, intellectual, or methodological—and hold the potential to reshape knowledge, policy, or society. The Prize supports scholars whose work is original, rigorous, impactful, and courageous—even when it is unpopular. 

Award

◦$1,000,000 awarded over five years
◦Flexible, largely unrestricted support
◦Expect 3-5 awards a year 

Selection Criteria:

◦Intellectual Independence
◦Non-Conformist Ideas
◦Impact and Vindication 

Other Parameters:

◦Limited to work in the Social Sciences.
◦Only living nominees will be considered.
◦Candidates must be citizens or legal residents of the United States.
◦The Carob Trust Prize for Academic Courage will take a nominee’s life’s work into account. Scholars who are earlier in their careers might be considered for a smaller prize.  
Timeline

◦Nov. 1: Nomination window closes
◦Spring: Annual Carob Trust Prize Award Ceremony 
Spirit of the Prize: 

Breakthroughs often begin as unpopular ideas. By honoring those who show independence, courage, and resilience, the Carob Trust Prize ensures that today’s controversial insights have the chance to become tomorrow’s common sense.

Bitcoin dumps on golden crosses are normal.

What is more telling is the bounce after the golden cross dump is over.

In 2019/2023, Bitcoin dumped into the golden cross then put in a higher high, thus confirming the end of the bear market.

In 2014/2015, Bitcoin dumped into the golden cross, then put in a lower high, and the bear market continued.

A higher high (if achieved) would likely correspond to a weekly close above the 50W SMA (which is a good predictor of the bear market being over).

A lower high (rejected at the 50W) would be a sign that the Q4 low occurs right on schedule.

To summarize:

The dump BTC is experiencing right now has happened previously in bear markets and in the beginning of bull markets. The thing to watch for whether the low is behind us is after this dump is over, does Bitcoin print a higher high (and go above the 50W) or a lower high (rejected again).

Once that data point arrives, it would likely be the nail in the coffin for either the bull or the bear case.

The piece is about DeSci, decentralized science.

Every institution stagnates the same way. A small group ends up controlling the agenda, that group gets invested in the current framework, and challenging the consensus becomes a career risk. I have watched it in banking, telecom, rocketry, and now science.

After 40 years I boiled it down to two rules.

1- The Draper Equation: the likelihood that a society needs to rethink an industry is proportional to the number of people benefiting from existing theories without change.

2- The Draper Corollary: the more centralized the decision-making, the less innovation occurs. The more decentralized the operations, the more innovation occurs and the faster that sector grows.

The consensus mocked Hotmail, Skype, Tesla, Bitcoin, and SpaceX too. Every time, mockery was an excellent signal.

Read the full editorial: https://t.co/kMYEnjkQTc

1/ first off must read, good compilation of projects ; really good alpha gathering here

2/ secondly from markets perspective i find that lending & borrowing is a very much solved primitive and as such new protocols dont really have much moat especially when entrenched winners move over. i mean lending, borrowing, yield - not only are these verticals solved, they're also sorely based on antifragility - w all the hacks going on, no one wants to put serious money into a protocol 2 weeks old. 

theres also no real new innovation to be done here; hence no new earnings inflection on top of existing defi revenue. 

3/ as such i dont really view lending borrowing tokens net new nor interesting

with uniswap on the chain though, i think an aggregator makes alot more sense than a standalone dex. 

5/ stock token pairs are very much memes - i dont think theres any new innovative layers here. at best i believe these will trade like beta to the underlying, at worst i dont see a key differential bw token1 paired to stockXYZ and token2 paired to the same stock. 

and so the framework to approach this is w akin to memes - all an attention game

sometimes you just have to take a chance
